result.summary: The image shows a typical residential street with row houses and continuous sidewalks on both sides. While sidewalks provide basic pedestrian access, the lack of marked crossings and the presence of continuous on-street parking create visibility challenges for pedestrians wishing to cross the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians, particularly children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Lack of designated crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian refuge areas visible, forcing pedestrians to cross the wide roadway unprotected.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to reduce crossing distance and move pedestrians into the driver's line of sight beyond the parked cars.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Mark crossings with high-visibility paint to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Speed Humps
interventions.description: Implement vertical speed control measures to maintain low vehicle speeds appropriate for a residential street.

result.summary: This residential street features row houses with a sidewalk on the far side, but lacks visible pedestrian infrastructure on the near side. There are no marked crossings or traffic calming measures visible, and parked cars create potential sightline obstructions for pedestrians attempting to cross the two-lane roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossing
hazards.description: There are no designated or marked areas for pedestrians to cross the street safely between intersections.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the center of the roadway

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb can block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, especially children, who might step into the street.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility (continental) marked crosswalk to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides within a residential row-house context, providing basic pedestrian access. However, the lack of marked crossings, presence of visual obstructions from parked cars and vegetation, and a wide roadway design create a moderately risky environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without designated markings or priority in a residential area.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway between the residential blocks

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and overgrown vegetation on the right side of the street obscure visibility between pedestrians and drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curbsides where parked cars and tall bushes are located

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at potential crossing points to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crossings with high-visibility patterns to alert drivers to pedestrian presence and establish right-of-way.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds in this residential context.

result.summary: The image shows a residential row-house street with a continuous concrete sidewalk that lacks a physical buffer from the roadway. The pedestrian environment is basic, with visible pavement degradation and a lack of safety-enhancing features like street trees or lighting.

hazards.name: Uneven Pavement
hazards.description: The sidewalk exhibits significant cracking and uneven slabs, creating potential trip hazards for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground sidewalk area in front of the houses

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: There is no physical separation or buffer zone between the walking area and the vehicle travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: The interface between the sidewalk and the roadway

interventions.title: Sidewalk Rehabilitation
interventions.description: Repair and level the concrete sidewalk slabs to provide a smooth, ADA-compliant walking surface.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strip
interventions.description: Introduce a planting buffer between the curb and the sidewalk to provide physical separation from traffic and improve the microclimate.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and personal security for pedestrians during nighttime hours.
